audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer reads Skill on rows 0-4 and Ryze on rows 5-6; content win[] and the packet chart both read Karma through row 5 with only row 6 going to Ryze.
audit.why: Ryze has no burst before mana items and has to close to 615 to land Spell Flux or Rune Prison, so every laning row is Karma's. At 50.77% over 65 games the swing is late, not at first item.
audit.corrected: phases[0..5].side to Karma; row 6 already agrees on both layers.

audit.why: Level 6 genuinely does not spike Ryze in lane — Realm Warp is a 180/160/140s portal with no damage — and the content layer already says so. The real spike is a completed mana build, which the content layer places at two items.
audit.corrected: No change; phases[5].why already describes Karma's item window and now matches a Karma-sided row.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns holds no digit, and the page calls Rune Prison a "point-blank root" without the condition that makes it one.
audit.why: Riot's text says Rune Prison damages and slows, and roots only if the target already has Flux on it. Spell Flux is 615 range on 2.5-3.5s and his other basic abilities reset Overload, so the whole combo is E-first — staying outside 615 removes the root entirely and leaves only a 1000-range Overload.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field carries W 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 at 615, E 2.5-3.5s and R 180/160/140; the Flux condition is stated in dosFull[0].d and report[5].t.

edits.before: Ryze wins by landing Rune Prison (Root), denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Ryze wins by sticking Spell Flux on you first, turning Rune Prison into a root, and out-scaling you once his mana stacks.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): matchup-defining — Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your RE shield-speed like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rune Prison: 11s at rank 1, 9s maxed, 615 range — it only roots if Spell Flux is already on you, otherwise it is a slow. - Spell Flux is 2.5-3.5s and resets Overload, so his combo is E-first. - Realm Warp is 180/160/140 and deals no damage.

edits.before: Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: The root needs Flux first — at 950 you sit outside his 615 E and it never lands.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, and on real windows RQ-W: the chunk plus tether-root turns a poke trade into a kill setup — E out before the answer.
edits.after: Your Q reaches 950 and his Overload 1000, but Spell Flux is only 615 — hold that gap and only the Q can reach you at all.

edits.before: Ryze spends Rune Prison (Root) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Rune Prison spent means 9-11s where his root cannot start and only Overload reaches.

edits.before: That is Ryze’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Bonus mana becomes damage for him — even farm scales.

edits.before: Spending Mantra on wave-clear while behind on poke — Karma without RQ banked is a support who took mid's farm.
edits.after: With items his Spell Flux into Overload rotation lands inside 615 range before your 8-10s shield returns.

edits.before: Track Ryze’s Rune Prison (Root): Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Ryze’s Rune Prison (Root): it only roots through Spell Flux, and his E is 615 range. Forward steps wait for its downtime.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — the RQ chunk cycles every 30 seconds. Chip him below half and hold the kill window.
edits.after: Lost Chapter timing — the RQ chunk cycles every 30s. Chip him below half from outside his 615-range E.

edits.before: No new ult — your 6 is a Mantra rank: faster cycles, bigger RQs. Press the early lead before scaling lanes wake up.
edits.after: Realm Warp is a 180s portal with no damage, so 6 changes nothing in lane. Your 6 is a Mantra rank — keep pressing.

notes: Chart proposed as one atomic group. The full layer was moved onto the content/packet values, which already agree with each other, so no paired win[N] edit is proposable — win[0..6] already hold the target strings and an edit would fail the exact-before check. Ratings left untouched (could not determine whether phases[N].rating is owner-favourability or matchup severity), which does leave phases[5] reading side=Karma with a 7/10 rating and phases[6] at 8/10. Content layer here is already matchup-specific and factually consistent with the kit, so it needed no edits. The focus token "Rune Prison (Root)" is technically conditional — it roots only through Flux — but it follows the AbilityName (Effect) convention and appears in many fields, so I corrected the prose around it rather than the token itself.
